rounds.proof_sketch: batch_size=16, channels=32 → total_output_elements = 512 * spatial_dims, always divisible by 256. num_blocks = total_output_elements/256 exactly. Max reachable linear_idx = (num_blocks-1)*256 + 255 = total_output_elements - 1. Condition 'linear_idx >= N' and 'linear_idx > N' both evaluate false for all reachable indices.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary check from '>=' to '>' for detecting when linear_idx exceeds the valid output range. However, with the fixed input shape (batch_size=16, channels=32), total_output_elements is always a multiple of 256 (since 16*32=512=2*256). This means the CUDA grid is sized exactly to cover all output elements with no leftover threads. The maximum linear_idx any thread can compute is total_output_elements-1, so neither the original condition (>=N) nor the mutated condition (>N) ever evaluates to true. The mutation is semantically equivalent under this configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The boundary condition is unreachable because the product batch_size*channels=512 ensures total_output_elements is always divisible by elements_per_block=256, meaning the grid exactly covers the output with no out-of-bounds thread indices.
rounds.recommendations: When testing boundary mutations in GPU kernels, verify whether the boundary is reachable by analyzing the relationship between launch configuration (threads_per_block, blocks) and the total work items. Fixed shapes that produce work sizes divisible by block sizes can make boundary guards unreachable.
